housing.summary: Frankfurt has one of Germany's tightest and most expensive rental markets, driven by its banking sector. Apartments are typically unfurnished (often without kitchens/light fixtures). Tenants usually pay a deposit (Kaution) of up to three months' cold rent held in a separate account, and many rentals require a Schufa credit report and proof of income. A Schufa-based letting agent commission may apply, though since 2015 the Bestellerprinzip means the party who hires the agent pays the fee.

banking.summary: Opening a German bank account (Girokonto) generally requires a passport/ID, proof of registered address (Meldebescheinigung from the Bürgeramt), and often a residence permit and proof of income or employment. Both traditional branch banks and app-based banks operate; SEPA transfers and the Girocard debit system are standard.

schools.summary: Frankfurt hosts a large international community and a wide range of international schools offering IB, British, American, French and other curricula, alongside German state schools (Grundschule, Gymnasium). Placement in international schools is competitive and fee-paying; state schooling is free but taught in German.

legal_admin.summary: Newcomers must register their residence (Anmeldung) at a local Bürgeramt within roughly two weeks of moving in, presenting a passport, rental contract and a landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung). Registration produces a Meldebescheinigung needed for banking, tax and other services. Non-EU nationals additionally need a residence permit from the Ausländerbehörde.
legal_admin.registration_step: Anmeldung (residence registration) at the Bürgeramt within ~14 days, with Wohnungsgeberbestätigung from the landlord

tax_finance.summary: After registration, residents are issued a tax identification number (Steuer-Identifikationsnummer / Steuer-ID) by post, required for employment and payroll. Income tax is withheld at source via wage tax (Lohnsteuer) based on tax classes (Steuerklassen); annual tax returns are filed with the Finanzamt.

transport.summary: Frankfurt has an extensive integrated public transport network of U-Bahn, S-Bahn, trams and buses coordinated within the RMV regional tariff association. Monthly tickets are available, and the nationwide Deutschlandticket offers unlimited regional/local travel. Healthcare requires enrolment in statutory (gesetzliche) or private health insurance, mandatory for residents and usually arranged via the employer.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences are valid; many non-EU licences must be exchanged for a German licence, sometimes requiring theory/practical tests depending on the country of issue
transport.healthcare_registration: Mandatory enrolment in statutory (GKV) or private (PKV) health insurance; register with a Krankenkasse, typically via the employer
